note: fx/fy are device-reported. cx/cy were measured, not taken from the device: at food_detect_start (camera straight down) three UNOCCLUDED berries were located in both the depth sensor and the colour frame and each gave the principal point under the factory depth->colour extrinsic, agreeing to +-9 px (cx) and +-3.5 px (cy); 1 px is ~0.34 mm at berry depth. This is a constant of the camera, so it is frozen here rather than re-estimated each run -- re-estimating it from whatever fruit is in view made an intrinsic depend on the fruit, and a half-occluded berry dragged cy by 24 px. locate_target checks every run's correspondences against it instead. The factory cy is NOT wrong -- within 13 px; cy/h = 0.33 is simply an off-centre 16:9 crop of the 4:3 sensor.
vertical_vp_note: Image of TRUE VERTICAL at food_detect_start, measured 2026-09-23: the tool was moved straight down 30/60/90 mm with orientation held to 0.01 deg, SIFT features on the table and mat were matched between heights, and every true match slides along a line through one point. RANSAC + least squares: (657.6, 236.6) +- 0.3 px, 67-79% of matches consistent, spread across the frame, implied depth 0.441 m (IQR 0.430-0.456, agreeing with the depth sensor). 11 px from the optical centre = the camera looks 0.48 deg off vertical, i.e. the tool's own 0.58 deg tilt. The utensil tip's vertical line projects THROUGH THIS POINT, not through (cx, cy). A ~3 deg camera tilt was hypothesised to explain a large miss and is ruled out by this.
